caveat: Hours above the threshold outside July–September are not counted, so each 1% value is a mild underestimate. The same underestimate applies to a block and to its station, so the difference between them is unaffected.
modelBiasCheck: At ladder thresholds set from the season maximum, NOAA measured zero hours in July at coastal stations where the model reports 7-16. That is the documented coastal warm bias (+4.3F mean) expressed as hours. The atlas compares a modelled block against a modelled station, so a shared bias cancels; the residual is the model compressing the coast-inland gradient, which makes 10.1% an underestimate rather than an inflated figure.
coverage: 1,238 of 1,761 San Diego cells resolved. The rest had their 88-hour crossing outside the three-rung ladder and are excluded rather than extrapolated.
scope: San Diego only. The API key ran out of credits before Los Angeles and Fresno ladders could be fetched, so those metros remain on the July-maximum basis.
